mobbin:e7700240-0fb3-4a8b-aa81-7a640b1aa.summary: The user picks strength and improvement tags, waits up to about 30 seconds for FeedbackAI, then chooses one of three AI drafts to edit.
steps: Strengths and Opportunities tags: custom, select up to 2
Tags and Examples fields for selected traits
FeedbackAI loading, up to 30 seconds
Choose suggestion: 3 AI drafts, Generate new
Suggestion list: drafts include custom-tag phrasing
Suggestion selected with green check, ready for Next
steal: Tag fields, with a limit of two areas to improve, narrow what the AI writes about before it starts (screens 1 to 2).
The loading text says it can take up to 30 seconds and shows placeholder bars, so the wait is expected (screen 3).
The user chooses from three suggestions or asks for new ones, so a person picks the tone before editing (screens 4 to 6).
A note under the card says the text comes from GPT-3, so readers know the formative feedback is AI-written (screens 3 to 6).
avoid: The AI drafts repeat playful custom tags ('good potato') in the feedback; clinical wording has to be checked and tied to competencies (screens 5 to 6).
mobbin:e7700240-0fb3-4a8b-aa81-7a640b1aa.fit: Reports: an AI-drafted formative note for faculty, written from competency tags. It adds to Responses and Skill Development, not to accreditation packs.

mobbin:560e3cdd-be36-4bf6-a0f1-8ca6fe968.summary: From the open 360 reviews, the user writes an anonymous peer review from chosen adjectives, lets FeedbackAI draft the text, reviews and submits it, and sees '1 of 2' progress.
steps: 360 Open Reviews: Give Peer Review and progress bar
Anonymous Reviews: How it works and Let's do this
Questionnaire: adjective labels and Generate Feedback
Tags selected (helpful, team player)
AI narrative filled in rich-text editor
More competency sections collapsed; Saved draft
Review and Submit: tags and narratives per competency
Review and Submit footer: Back and Submit
Success window: Nice work and Shared successfully
Dashboard: 1 of 2 reviews submitted progress
steal: A 'How it works' screen explains that chosen adjectives feed FeedbackAI and that peers stay anonymous, so privacy and the AI's role are clear before starting (screen 2).
'Generate Feedback' drafts text from the chosen adjectives, and the user is asked to 'sprinkle in specific examples' (screens 3 to 5).
A review screen gathers the tags and text for every competency before 'Submit' (screens 7 to 8).
After sending, the person who asked for reviews sees a '1 of 2 reviews submitted' progress bar (screens 1 and 10).
avoid: An emoji and GIF toolbar in the feedback editor is too casual for summative clinical reports (screens 5 to 6).
mobbin:560e3cdd-be36-4bf6-a0f1-8ca6fe968.fit: Reports: an AI write-up of formative feedback from peers or faculty, based on competency labels. Pooling answers anonymously fits reports with several raters per skill, not room-use numbers.

mobbin:f2d6fb5a-36ee-4c5c-9612-55be9bbd3.summary: The user picks an AI suggestion, edits it and submits, then sees the feedback marked 'Jon hasn't seen this yet', with Edit and Delete still available.
steps: Choose AI suggestion, one selected
Edit and send: editable draft and Submit Feedback
1:1 Feedback and Kudos: unseen feedback card
Feed: unseen status with Edit, Delete, Comment
steal: The chosen draft opens for editing before 'Submit', so AI text is never sent automatically (screens 1 to 2).
A 'hasn't seen this yet' status on the shared feedback shows whether it has been read (screens 3 to 4).
Edit and Delete stay available until it is read, so faculty can take feedback back before the learner opens it (screens 3 to 4).
mobbin:f2d6fb5a-36ee-4c5c-9612-55be9bbd3.fit: Reports: a faculty note written after the AI draft, with control over when it is seen. Useful for formative learner reports before PDFs are shared with deans.
